summary.oneLiner: KOEL delivered record Q4 standalone sales of INR1,522cr (+24% YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR5,604cr (+25% YoY), driven by 41% volume growth in Powergen (vs 18% industry) and 37% international sales growth, while margin expansion to 13.1% EBITDA margin and INR1,400cr capex for HHP capacity signal structural scaling toward its $2B FY30 target.
summary.business: KOEL manufactures air-cooled and liquid-cooled engines and diesel generator sets from 1 kW to 10 MW, and industrial engines from 20 hp to 13,500 hp, supplying construction, earth-moving, marine, mining, railways, fluid handling and agricultural applications in both domestic and international markets. Its portfolio spans powergen, industrial engines, firefighting systems, farm equipment, electric motors and fluid solutions, sold into residential, telecom, infrastructure, defence, hospitality, data center, manufacturing, mining, agriculture and fisheries end-users. Following the October 2025 slump sale of the Business-to-Customer Water Management Solutions business to wholly owned subsidiary KOEL Fluid Dynamics Private Limited, the Company has sharpened its focus on core B2B Power & Energy segments, complemented by the Fluid Dynamics segment and the Arka Group financial-services businesses.

currentContext.strategies: Long-term '2B2B' roadmap to reach $2 billion consolidated revenue (₹16,000 crores) by FY 29-30, sequenced as Core (FY 25-26), Develop (FY 26-27), Expand (FY 27-28) and Novel (FY 28-29).|FY 25-26 'Core' phase focused on execution of the manufacturing strategy and on capacity utilisation of the fluid dynamics business.|FY 26-27 'Develop' phase focused on complete execution of the technology roadmap and on increasing the share of business of Arka Retail.|FY 27-28 'Expand' phase focused on inorganic growth opportunities in line with core strategies, increasing international market share and improving market share in the fluid dynamics segment.|FY 28-29 'Novel' phase focused on improving share of business in defence and retail, expanding into non-ICE programmes in line with the core business, and completing the fluid dynamics product portfolio.|For the upcoming fiscal year, pivoting towards high-value engineering, digital manufacturing and a fuel-agnostic product portfolio to capture emerging demand in India and overseas; FY 25-26 strategic focus centred on high-margin segments, energy transition and global expansion.|Sharpened the B2B focus by transferring the B2C business to 100% subsidiary KOEL Fluid Dynamics Pvt. Ltd. by way of slump sale, concentrating the parent on core B2B Power & Energy segments.|Structural entry into defence and railways through incorporation of wholly owned subsidiary Kirloskar Advanced Systems Pvt. Ltd.|Inorganic strengthening of Powergen and Industrial Engines through the announced 100% acquisition of KTSPL, aimed at more customer-focused solutions.|Fuel-agnostic technology strategy: engines and gensets on biodiesel, natural gas, Hydrogen Fuel Enhanced Combustion (HFEC), ethanol, methanol, HVO, hythane, hydrogen-diesel blend, pure hydrogen, isobutanol and biogas, backed by in-house R&D that enables complete development and compliance with stringent emission and noise norms.|Building a green-energy export position: secured IP and patents for India's first hydrogen-engine-based gensets, positioning KOEL for entry into European and North American green energy markets.|Data center vertical build-out via the Optiprime platform with certified DCCP ratings up to 2,400 kW for mission-critical applications, alongside the world's smallest 1,000 kVA gensets launched for MENA and North American markets.|Differentiation through digital/connected products and service reach — operating the largest fleet of IoT-enabled gensets and a service network of over 500 outlets, embedding sustainability across operations and offerings.|Portfolio breadth across powergen, industrial engines, firefighting systems, farm equipment, electric motors and fluid solutions, serving residential, telecom, infrastructure, defence, hospitality, data centers, manufacturing, mining, agriculture and fisheries, with engines from 1 kW to 10 MW.|Dividend philosophy is codified: pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations the Board has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy, which is published on the Company's website, and the practice is a two-tranche distribution each year - an interim dividend declared by the Board during the year plus a final dividend recommended to members for approval at the AGM (dividend paid subject to tax deduction at source). Retention is the default for the balance: no appropriation was made to the General Reserve, with the residual profit carried forward, so internally generated surplus stays available to fund the growth agenda rather than being locked into reserves. Capital allocation is run as a formal framework embedded in the integrated Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) architecture, alongside the delegation-of-authority matrix, internal financial controls and enterprise risk management, with Board and committee oversight; the Company also states that it aligns capital expenditure and R&D priorities with its climate objectives and energy-transition roadmap. Reinvestment intent under the Vision 2B2B framework is directed at the technology roadmap (alternate fuels, emission-compliant and modular platforms, digital integration), premium high-horsepower capacity for data-centre and infrastructure demand, maximising capacity utilisation and completing the B2C product portfolio (now housed in the wholly owned subsidiary KFD), building out the international arm (including funding subsidiary KIME's working capital and its acquisition of a promoter-group trading entity), expansion into non-ICE programmes such as energy storage and electrification, and - from FY 27-28 - inorganic M&A aligned with core competencies, with the financial-services subsidiaries (AFHPL/Arka Fincap) held as material subsidiaries within the Group structure.|BRSR Core disclosures carry Reasonable Assurance from an external assurance provider (BDO India Services Private Limited) — the highest BRSR assurance tier, indicating externally verified sustainability data rather than self-declared metrics.|Alternative-fuel and green-energy product strategy as the core decarbonisation commitment: secured IP and patents for India's first hydrogen-engine-based gensets, certification for India's first CPCB IV+ 58.5 kVA HCNG genset and first CPCB IV+ 2.4 kW LPG genset, and in-house development of KOEL's first alkaline electrolyser stack.|Proposal to CPCB for acceptance of raw biogas as an alternate fuel for genset applications in India — a regulatory-pathway initiative to open a renewable fuel category for the core product line.|Advanced-engineering commitment to integrate renewable energy, conventional fossil-fuel generation, battery storage and intelligent power management to maximise fuel utilisation and ensure uninterrupted power supply; technology tracks span internal combustion engines, energy storage, electrification, fuel cells and electrolysers.|Ethanol-based gensets for telecom markets and LPG gensets for households/retailers, plus scaling of the BS-V product portfolio — moving the emissions profile of the installed base, not just the flagship range.|Planned rollout of an AI-powered Video Analytics System across manufacturing facilities using AI and computer vision for real-time monitoring, early hazard detection and proactive risk management, as a workplace-safety commitment.|Sustained external recognition on energy and resource management: Apex India Green Leaf Platinum for both Energy Management and Water Management, CII National Award 'Excellent Energy Efficient Unit' for three consecutive years and 'National Energy Leader', and Gold (three consecutive years) then Diamond in the India Green Manufacturing Challenge.|Integrated Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) framework with Enterprise Risk Management, Risk Management Committee and Audit Committee oversight, periodic Board and committee evaluations, and an established vigil/whistle-blower mechanism.|KOEL IP Policy effective 1 February 2026 plus an Inventor Rewards & Recognition Programme, institutionalising innovation governance alongside record patent (8) and design (14) filings for the year.|Diversity representation disclosed at leadership level — women comprise 27.27% of the Board of Directors and 33.33% of Key Management Personnel; permanent-worker attrition held at 0.0% in FY 2026.|Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for every stakeholder group (communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers, value-chain partners), with a dedicated sustainability contact channel (sustainability@kirloskar.com).
currentContext.expansion: The FY 2025-26 annual report frames KOEL's expansion less as brick-and-mortar capacity addition and more as structural re-architecting of the group and of the product platform. The most concrete corporate-structure step was the incorporation of a new wholly owned subsidiary, Kirloskar Advanced Systems Private Limited (KASPL), Pune: the Board approved its incorporation at its meeting on 11th February, 2026 and the company was incorporated on 30th March, 2026, with no commercial operations carried out up to 31st March, 2026 — so the vehicle is created and its ramp lies ahead in FY 2026-27. In parallel, the Board at its 10th October, 2025 meeting approved the transfer of the Company's Business-to-Customer (B2C) segment, i.e. Water Management Solutions (WMS) — Domestic & Exports Business — by way of slump sale as a going concern to wholly owned subsidiary KOEL Fluid Dynamics Private Limited (KFD, formerly La-Gajjar Machineries Private Limited), consideration being the issuance and allotment of equity shares of KFD to the Company on a private placement basis under a Business Transfer Agreement executed on 10th October, 2025; the transfer took effect from 11th October, 2025. This carves the B2C water/pumps franchise into a dedicated platform (Fluid Dynamics) while KOEL standalone concentrates on engines and power solutions. International reach was extended through Kirloskar International ME FZE, UAE (KIME), incorporated 7th January, 2025 as a wholly owned subsidiary, which had no commercial operations up to 31st March, 2025 and moved into operations during FY 2025-26; the US presence runs through Kirloskar Americas Corporation and step-down entity Engines LPG, LLC dba Wildcat Power Gen. On the product-platform side, the Company describes manufacturing air-cooled and liquid-cooled engines for generator sets spanning 1 kW to 10 MW and supplying engines into construction, earth-moving, marine, mining, railways, fluid handling and agricultural applications — a deliberately wide band that the report positions as the base for further coverage. The capability build-out that management foregrounds is fuel-agnostic: an alternative-fuel portfolio covering biodiesel, natural gas, Hydrogen Fuel Enhanced Combustion (HFEC), ethanol, methanol, Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO), hythane, hydrogen-diesel blend, pure hydrogen, isobutanol and biogas-based engines. This is tied directly to the regulatory runway the MD&A lays out: CPCB IV+ became mandatory in July 2024 for gensets up to 800 kW and its full implementation mandates sharp cuts in particulate matter and NOx, accelerating the shift to CRDI systems, after-treatment solutions and dual-fuel configurations; CEV Stage V tightens construction-equipment norms while TREM Stage V tractor timelines were deferred; and the NCR's 70% gas-based dual-fuel requirement pulls the mix toward cleaner fuels. Demand-side anchors cited for this expansion are data centres and AI workloads (Indian data-centre/digital-infrastructure demand scaling from 1.5 GW in 2025 to 6.5 GW by 2030), railway and metro modernisation needing advanced standby and prime power, defence indigenisation, and grid firming as renewables installed capacity reached 178 GW with 44.5 GW added in 2025. The Fluid Dynamics opportunity is framed as a shift of the Indian pump market — still about 70% agricultural and residential — towards higher-margin industrial segments, solar adoption and IoT integration. No specific new plant, greenfield site, line commissioning date or capacity-tonnage target is disclosed in the routed sections.

pace.|Management flags that although the Indian economic environment is expected to support this growth, there are looming threats of a potential global slowdown due to continued geopolitical risks.

risks.risk: Regulatory and emission-norm compliance in the engineering/powergen business
risks.note: Management calls the transition to stricter emission norms a 'non-negotiable hurdle'. Failure to align the product portfolio with evolving standards carries a triple threat — statutory penalties, direct revenue loss from barred sales, and long-term erosion of KOEL's premium brand equity. Because certification is product-by-product (CPCB IV+ etc.), a lag in any platform can strand inventory in the primary revenue segment.

risks.risk: Supply chain resilience for critical raw materials and specialised components
risks.note: High-precision engineering depends on a stable supply chain; any disruption in procurement of critical raw materials or specialised components immediately jeopardises production timelines and operational efficiency. This is a throughput risk on the segment that drives the bulk of revenue, and it sits largely outside management control.

risks.risk: Innovation and competitive differentiation as rivals move to hybrid and alternative fuels
risks.note: Global and local players are rapidly adopting hybrid and alternative-fuel technologies, and management states KOEL must sustain its 'differentiation edge' to prevent market share dilution. The company's answer — hydrogen/HCNG/LPG gensets, electrolysers, fuel cells, Optiprime hybrids — is R&D-heavy and unproven at scale, so the risk is that spend does not convert into a durable technology lead.

risks.risk: Market fragmentation and price competition in Fluid Dynamics (water management)
risks.note: The segment faces a high density of unorganised players, leading to aggressive price wars that put constant pressure on margins despite KOEL's superior distribution network and brand heritage. Structural — it caps pricing power in the consumer-facing business regardless of brand strength.

risks.risk: Climatic/monsoon sensitivity of Fluid Dynamics revenue
risks.note: Revenue in the FD segment is intrinsically linked to rainfall patterns; an inconsistent monsoon causes significant volatility in demand for pump sets and agricultural equipment, which management says makes y-o-y revenue forecasting a challenge. This introduces an exogenous, non-diversifiable swing factor into group revenue visibility.

risks.risk: Execution risk in the strategic realignment of the B2C/water business into KOEL Fluid Dynamics
risks.note: The standalone FD business (Water Management Solutions, domestic and exports) was transferred by slump sale to wholly owned subsidiary KOEL Fluid Dynamics Pvt. Ltd. (formerly La-Gajjar Machineries) with effect from 11 October 2025, and is now reported as discontinued operations at standalone level. The move is intended to unlock operational synergies and give dedicated retail focus — but the promised synergies and the retail competitiveness are yet to be demonstrated, and the reporting break reduces comparability.

risks.risk: Governance and compliance strain from scaling into a diversified, global energy-solutions group
risks.note: The BRSR flags Corporate Governance as a material risk-and-opportunity: scale and complexity of operations have increased across geographies, subsidiaries and regulatory environments (including new entities such as Kirloskar Advanced Systems Pvt. Ltd., Kirloskar Americas, KIME UAE and the Arka financial-services arms). Failure to keep governance aligned with evolving regulation could bring compliance, reputational or operational exposure and higher legal costs.

risks.risk: Business-ethics and third-party conduct risk across a broad partner network
risks.note: KOEL engages a wide network of employees, suppliers, customers and channel partners across domestic and international markets. Management explicitly flags that an ethical lapse — conflicts of interest, bribery, fraud, misuse of information or Code of Conduct breach — could adversely affect business continuity and stakeholder confidence. Mitigation rests on Code of Conduct, related-party/insider-trading policies, whistle-blower channels and Audit/Ethics Committee oversight.

one-line thesis: KOEL delivered record Q4 standalone sales of INR1,522cr (+24% YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR5,604cr (+25% YoY), driven by 41% volume growth in Powergen (vs 18% industry) and 37% international sales growth, while margin expansion to 13.1% EBITDA margin and INR1,400cr capex for HHP capacity signal structural scaling toward its $2B FY30 target.
financial scorecard: revenue: +25% YoY (FY26); EBITDA/margin: +33% YoY to INR737cr, margin +90bps to 13.1% (no distortions); PAT (rptd): +35% YoY to INR464cr; PAT (normalized): same as reported (no exceptional items); order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash position of INR552cr
guidance: revenue growth: targeting $2B by FY30; margin: committed to sustaining 13%+ EBITDA margin; order inflow: not quantified; capex/commissioning: INR1,400cr over FY27-FY28 for 20,000 HHP units at Kagal, with 50,000 unit capacity enhancement (INR700cr) operational by Apr'27
segment / subsidiary detail: Powergen: 32% YoY growth, 50,000 units sold (41% vs 18% industry); Industrial: 22% YoY growth, led by construction (+44%); Aftermarket: 15% YoY growth; International: 37% YoY growth, crossed INR1,000cr gross sales; Financial Services (Arka): AUM up 10% to INR7,947cr, PAT stable at INR69cr
growth verticals / optionality: HHP segment (up to 6.3MW gensets for NPCIL), data center Edge/Colo/hyperscaler demand, gas/methanol/hydrogen engine readiness, and systems integration via Kirloskar Advanced Systems
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 90bps to 13.1% despite commodity inflation; pricing adjustments made periodically but not quantified; operating leverage expected to improve from FY27 as capex ramps and sales scale
capex / expansion: INR1,400cr over FY27-FY28 for new HHP production line and building at Kagal (100% new capex); INR700cr already underway for 50,000 unit capacity enhancement (operational Apr'27); total gross block to reach ~INR4,000cr post-capex
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for HHP and international scalability; maintaining net cash position (INR552cr); Arka focused on AUM growth and retail secured lending; no dividend or buyback guidance provided
risks & watch-items: Commodity price volatility (copper, pig iron), geopolitical disruptions in Middle East (though no Q4 impact noted), execution risk on new HHP capacity, and slower-than-expected adoption of alternative fuel engines
management quality / tone: Confident, long-term oriented, disciplined; emphasized sustainable growth over quarterly spikes, strong belief in engineering capability, and commitment to $2B FY30 target; tone was strategic, not reactive
non-obvious takeaways: 1) 6.3MW gensets for NPCIL prove HHP capability beyond commercial norms; 2) INR1,400cr capex for 20,000 units implies ~INR70cr/unit vs INR14cr/unit for 50,000 units — reflects HHP complexity, not volume; 3) Netherlands subsidiary is a strategic vehicle for future energy transition products, not immediate revenue driver
